preamble: Depalatalization of the voiceless palatal stop [c] to the alveolar or dental stop [t] fronts the tongue contact and removes the palatal articulation. The clearest documented case is Egyptian: the Old Egyptian palatal ṯ /c/ (itself from palatalized *k) frequently merged with t from the end of the Old Kingdom onward, a change Peust calls palatal fronting, although many lexemes kept ṯ and later developed an affricate instead.

examples.note: Middle Egyptian paradigms already show tn alongside ṯn.
In Late Egyptian the t-forms became the normal spellings and the pronoun became common gender.
The Coptic reflexes show a dental stop where Old Egyptian had the palatal.
The palatal had become a dental stop by Middle Egyptian; Bohairic ⲛⲟⲩϯ (nouti) likewise has t.

sources: Allen, J. P. (2013). The Ancient Egyptian Language: An Historical Study. Cambridge University Press. https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9781139506090
